PullRequest.Title: Add opt-in auto-archive/delete inactive sessions with merged pull requests
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

This PR adds three lifecycle controls for agent sessions that have at least one merged pull request and no open related pull requests:

- `chat.agentSessions.autoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - disabled by default (`0`)
  - automatically archives inactive sessions after 1, 7, 15, or 30 days
- `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - disabled by default (`0`)
  - permanently deletes automatically archived sessions after a separate 1, 7, 15, or 30 day grace period
- `chat.agentSessions.autoRemoveWorktreesAfterMerge`
  - enabled by default
  - controls standalone cleanup when archive and deletion are both disabled
  - can be disabled to retain worktrees only while both record-cleanup settings remain disabled

### Setting precedence

`autoRemoveWorktreesAfterMerge` is only an opt-out for standalone worktree cleanup. Enabling automatic archive or deletion overrides it because those lifecycles require eligible worktrees to be removed. Removal still requires a branch with an upstream and known counts of zero outgoing commits and zero uncommitted changes; otherwise the lifecycle action is blocked rather than force-removing the worktree.

Each setting is application-scoped, tagged Preview, synchronized into Agent Host root configuration, and has its own enterprise policy:

- `ChatAgentSessionsAutoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays`
- `ChatAgentSessionsAutoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays`
- `ChatAgentSessionsAutoRemoveWorktreesAfterMerge`

## Lifecycle behavior

- lifecycle candidates are prefiltered from durable session metadata before restoring sessions
- active and external sessions are excluded
- every related pull request is refreshed authoritatively during candidate evaluation and again immediately before lifecycle side effects, so reopening a closed PR blocks the action
- cleanup-only candidates are revalidated and handled without restoring the session
- sessions whose worktree is already absent are filtered before pull request refresh
- archive/delete settings, session state, retention periods, and pull request identity are revalidated after session restoration
- automatic deletion applies only to sessions carrying durable automatic-archive provenance
- manually archived sessions are never made deletion-eligible by this lifecycle
- unarchiving clears automatic-archive provenance
- automatic archive uses the normal archive action and side-effect path, including provider notification
- deletion cleans a retained worktree inside the disposal critical section, where concurrent unarchive is rejected
- deletion uses the persisted primary repository root when removing checkpoint/review refs, including after worktree cleanup and Agent Host restart
- startup/hourly evaluation remains active when any one of the three behaviors is enabled

## Worktree cleanup safety

An inactive session's worktree is removed only after every related pull request is confirmed closed or merged, at least one is merged, and Git reports all of the following:

- the worktree has a branch
- the branch tracks an upstream
- outgoing and uncommitted change counts are both known
- there are zero outgoing commits
- there are zero uncommitted changes

Incoming commits do not block cleanup. For example, if the PR branch was updated from `main` on the remote after the local checkout was last synchronized, the local branch may be behind its upstream but has no local-only work to lose. If the histories diverged and Git reports outgoing commits, cleanup remains blocked.

Missing or unknown Git state fails closed. Cleanup uses ordinary, non-force `git worktree remove`, so Git performs a final dirty-worktree check as well. The lifecycle does not commit local changes or force-remove the worktree.

The standalone worktree setting applies only while archive and deletion are disabled. When a session has multiple related pull requests, none may be open and at least one must be merged before any automatic archive, deletion, or worktree cleanup occurs. Closed-unmerged PRs do not block cleanup once another related PR has merged:

| Pull requests | Archive | Delete | Remove worktrees | Result for an inactive session |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No related PR is open; at least one is merged | Off | Off | On (default) | Keep the session visible and undeleted; remove its worktree only when its branch tracks an upstream and Git reports known counts of zero outgoing commits and zero uncommitted changes |
| No related PR is open; at least one is merged | Off | Off | Off | Keep both the session and its worktree |
| No related PR is open; at least one is merged | On | Any | On or Off | Override the standalone toggle; after the inactivity threshold, archive only if the worktree branch tracks an upstream and Git reports known counts of zero outgoing commits and zero uncommitted changes |
| No related PR is open; at least one is merged | Any | On | On or Off | Override the standalone toggle; permanently delete only after any retained worktree meets the upstream, zero-outgoing-commit, and zero-uncommitted-change requirements and is removed |
| At least one related PR is open | Any | Any | Any | Take no lifecycle action; keep the session, archive state, and worktree unchanged |
| All related PRs are closed without merging | Any | Any | Any | Take no lifecycle action because the session has no merged PR |
| No related PRs | Any | Any | Any | Take no lifecycle action |

Removing a worktree is reversible for the retained session: the checkout can be recreated when the session is resumed.

## User experience when archive and delete are disabled

Both record-cleanup settings default to disabled, so the session remains visible, is not automatically archived, and is not permanently deleted.

With the default-on worktree setting, a safely synchronized worktree may still be reclaimed after merge. There is no separate confirmation prompt when that cleanup occurs. Users who want to retain the checkout can turn off `chat.agentSessions.autoRemoveWorktreesAfterMerge` while leaving both archive and deletion disabled.

The existing one-time **Turn On Session Cleanup** notification remains separate from worktree cleanup. It appears for an eligible merged-PR session after 15 days of inactivity while both record-cleanup settings are disabled. Its actions are:

- **Turn On Session Cleanup**: sets archive and delete thresholds to 15 days
- **Open Settings**: opens the `chat.agentSessions.auto*` settings

## Validation

- policy metadata generation
- client TypeScript type-check
- targeted ESLint for changed TypeScript files
- focused Agent Host lifecycle and candidate-enumeration tests
- `git diff --check`

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The two call sites, authoritative network implementation, serial candidate loop, default-enabled setting, and test-observed duplicate URL sequence are explicit. Exact request duration and typical candidate count vary, affecting severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: authoritative GitHub core API requests and API quota
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For C cleanup candidates whose P related PRs are all complete, each startup/hourly pass performs 2 × C × P authoritative requests instead of C × P; P is durably capped at 10, while C grows with retained worktree sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: doubled background network traffic, GitHub API-budget consumption, and lifecycle sweep latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no background lifecycle sweep or lifecycle-specific GitHub refresh for inactive worktree sessions.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new cleanup-only path first refreshes all related PRs at the top of _evaluateCandidate, performs only local settings/summary checks, and then refreshes the same URLs authoritatively again immediately before cleanup.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 164 calls _arePullRequestsComplete a second time on the cleanupWorktree branch after line 145 already completed the same authoritative check; cold cleanup candidates with no live summary skip even the intervening summary revalidation.
Findings.Title: Avoid refreshing every cleanup PR twice
Findings.Impact: With the default-on standalone worktree cleanup, Agent Host startup and every hourly pass issue two GitHub core reads per related PR for each merged/closed cleanup candidate. Users retaining many completed agent worktrees consume twice the required API quota and wait twice as long for the serialized cleanup sweep.
Findings.Evidence: _arePullRequestsComplete loops over every related URL and resolveForLifecycle creates a background subscription then calls subscription.refresh('core', ..., { authoritative: true }), which reaches the GitHub query boundary rather than accepting the cached snapshot. The lifecycle test's cleanup harness records restored: [] together with each pullRequestUrl appearing twice, confirming that cleanup candidates pay both complete refresh rounds without a restore between them. Candidates run serially in run(), so this also lengthens the pass directly.
Findings.Recommendation: Perform cleanup's local settings/summary revalidation first and make a single _arePullRequestsComplete call immediately before cleanup; keep the pre-restore check only for archive/delete candidates where restoration creates a meaningful intervening boundary.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The default setting, scheduler, unconditional cold-session branch, concrete stat/SQLite implementation, immediate disposal, and collection cardinality are all explicit. The number of retained sessions and platform-specific I/O duration vary, so magnitude affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem stats plus per-session SQLite connection opens, metadata queries, and closes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is one filesystem stat and, for existing data, one SQLite open/query/close for every unloaded internal registry entry (O(S) in retained session history), with only four operations in flight. It is paid even when a session has no PR or no worktree and is repeated hourly while cleanup remains enabled.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive background filesystem/database I/O and startup-time resource contention that grows with the user's session catalogue
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, Agent Host did not run a startup/hourly lifecycle pass over the durable session registry, so inactive unloaded sessions incurred no per-session database open for worktree cleanup.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The default-enabled cleanup pass enumerates all internal registered sessions. For an unloaded session `archived` is undefined, making this condition true unconditionally, so `tryOpenDatabase` runs before the code can reject sessions without related PR metadata or a worktree.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 2129 opens each entry's per-session database from inside the registered-session map. Because `cleanupWorktrees` defaults true, the earlier cutoff filters do not exclude recent unloaded sessions, and `archived === undefined` guarantees entry into this block.
Findings.Title: Do not reopen every session database on each cleanup pass
Findings.Impact: Users with large retained agent-session histories now get a catalogue-wide burst of filesystem and SQLite work after provider startup and on every hourly pass, including the common majority of sessions that have no lifecycle-relevant PR/worktree. This can contend with normal Agent Host startup and creates ongoing disk/CPU overhead.
Findings.Evidence: SessionDataService.tryOpenDatabase first performs a file-service stat, then acquires a SessionDatabase; the reference is disposed at the end of this block, and the reference collection closes the underlying database when the last reference is released. Thus cold sessions are not kept warm across passes. The added scheduler starts when a provider registers and reschedules every hour while cleanup is enabled, which it is by default. The lifecycle-candidate test also instruments tryOpenDatabase and confirms candidate enumeration opens cold session databases to discover metadata.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the minimal lifecycle eligibility facts in the existing durable session registry (or an equivalent invalidated candidate index) so the pass can select sessions with related PR/worktree metadata before opening per-session databases; retain the current per-session read as final authoritative validation only for selected candidates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Default-on standalone cleanup during Agent Host startup and hourly lifecycle passes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider registration schedules the pass immediately; normal UI startup does not await it, but candidate discovery and cleanup completion await registry enumeration, per-session metadata reads, authoritative PR checks, and Git safety/removal operations. The work can contend with other startup I/O.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List the global durable session registry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registry query per pass for all registered sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No lifecycle pass queried the registry for automatic merged-session cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before any cleanup candidate can be evaluated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat each cold session.db, open its SQLite database, read four metadata keys, then close it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat and up to one SQLite open/query/close for each unloaded internal registered session; limiter concurrency is 4. This includes sessions later rejected for having no related PR/worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inactive unloaded sessions were not opened by a scheduled cleanup sweep.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Candidate discovery waits for all queued session reads before returning any candidate list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the GitHub PR core fragment authoritatively.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For a cleanup candidate with P all-complete related PRs, 2P requests per pass; P is capped at 10. Open/failed PRs short-circuit earlier. Candidates are evaluated serially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No lifecycle-specific background PR requests occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both rounds must finish before Git worktree safety checks and removal begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Git branch-existence, status, remote, default-branch and possible divergence probes, then non-force worktree removal/verification when safe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one branch probe plus several Git-state probes per complete cleanup candidate; Git-state probes include three parallel commands and optional follow-ups. Removal adds one or more Git commands. Candidates remain serial, while probes within one candidate have limited parallelism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These checks/removal were not run automatically for inactive visible sessions unless a user archive action triggered the pre-existing archive cleanup path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines whether cleanup can complete; blocked worktrees remain for future hourly passes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: S retained internal sessions controls metadata I/O; C sessions with existing worktrees and related PRs controls network/Git work; P distinct related PR URLs per candidate is capped at 10 after normalization/deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Candidate metadata reads are limited to 4. Lifecycle candidates and their PR URLs are processed serially. Git-state probes for one candidate use Promise.all, and worktree mutations are sequenced per session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold session databases are opened and immediately released, so the next pass repeats the stat/open/query/close. PR resources can remain dormant briefly, but authoritative refreshes force network fetches and the cleanup path requests each URL twice. Successful worktree removal makes later isWorktreeCleanupNeeded checks negative; blocked worktrees are retried hourly.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: default enablement, immediate/hourly scheduling, database lifecycle, authoritative network calls, serial evaluation, and Git subprocess composition were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalogue sizes, filesystem speed, and number of retained merged worktrees vary. The O(S) database fan-out and exact duplicate 2P authoritative requests are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: one finding covers catalogue-wide per-session database fan-out, and one covers duplicate authoritative PR refreshes on cleanup-only candidates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opt-in automatic archival after the inactivity threshold
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The lifecycle pass must enumerate candidates, confirm all related PRs, restore each cold candidate, revalidate settings/state, confirm PRs again, then dispatch archive and persist automatic-archive provenance. Worktree cleanup is launched by the normal archive side-effect path and is not awaited by provenance persistence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read cold session metadata for threshold-eligible entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one per unloaded internal entry that cannot be rejected from live/registry facts; concurrency 4.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic archive candidate scan existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the candidate list is evaluated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authoritatively fetch each related PR core state before and after restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 2P successful complete-PR requests per archived candidate, with serial URL and candidate processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic archive validation traffic existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both rounds block archive; the intervening restore makes the second validation materially distinct.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the provider session and materialize host state, using registry and per-session/provider data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per cold archive candidate; existing in-flight restores coalesce per session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inactive sessions were restored only on explicit access/actions, not an automatic archive sweep.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Archive waits for restoration so normal action/side-effect semantics can be used.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata write per successfully archived session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The lifecycle candidate completes after provenance is durable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check Git safety and remove the worktree non-force when synchronized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One asynchronous worktree cleanup attempt per archive action, serialized per session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manual archive already invoked worktree cleanup; the diff changes safety checks and causes automatic archive actions to reach that existing side-effect path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the lifecycle run's awaited critical path because side effects attach a rejection handler without awaiting; still consumes background subprocess/I/O resources.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of sessions older than the configured cutoff, with P related PRs capped at 10 each.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Archive candidates and PRs are serial. Candidate metadata reads are limited to 4. Session restoration coalesces per session and residency bounds retained restored sessions. Worktree cleanup is sequenced per session but runs asynchronously relative to the lifecycle loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Registry/live summaries prefilter some entries. Cold metadata and PR authoritative reads are not reused across hourly passes; successful archive provenance prevents re-archival and enables later deletion. In-flight restores coalesce per session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and boundaries; no independent actionable regression beyond the shared catalogue scan was established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider restore cost varies substantially by provider/session, but archival is opt-in, threshold-filtered, serial, and semantically requires restoration in the current architecture.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: serial, thresholded, opt-in work and the second PR check surrounds a meaningful restore boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opt-in permanent deletion of automatically archived sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Candidate discovery and initial PR validation precede restoration. Conditional disposal then revalidates PRs, checks/removes any retained worktree, rechecks provenance/settings and PRs, invokes provider deletion, tombstones the registry entry, deletes session data/refs, and removes remaining worktree state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read archive/provenance/PR metadata during enumeration and revalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one per cold archived candidate during enumeration, plus provenance reads during restored revalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No scheduled automatic-deletion provenance reads existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks candidate selection and final deletion validation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authoritatively fetch related PR core states at initial evaluation and twice inside the disposal validation sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 3P requests for a successful delete candidate, serially, with P capped at 10; failures/open PRs short-circuit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic delete PR validation traffic existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All successful rounds block permanent deletion and preserve reopen safety.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider deletion occurred only on explicit session disposal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks host-side tombstone and data deletion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read worktree metadata, optionally run Git safety/removal, clean shared refs, delete per-session data, and verify worktree deregistration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per deletion candidate, with several Git commands when a retained worktree exists and additional ref cleanup per configured working directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deletion cleanup boundaries existed for explicit deletion, but the diff newly invokes them from the automatic lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations are inside the disposal critical section and block deletion completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Automatically archived sessions older than the delete cutoff, multiplied by up to 10 related PRs and retained worktrees/working directories.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Deletion candidates and PRs are serial. Disposal is guarded per session; worktree operations are sequenced per session. No cross-candidate burst occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Automatic-archive provenance is durable and unarchive clears it. Authoritative PR reads bypass freshness reuse. Successful deletion removes registry/data state; blocked deletion retries on later hourly passes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the boundaries and serial critical path; the repeated validations protect deletion semantics, and no separate high-confidence performance defect was established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Deletion candidate counts should normally be small and settings are opt-in; provider and repository cleanup durations vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the shared candidate-scan issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: One-time renderer prompt to enable archive/delete cleanup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing per-session PR polling populates the PR model. The added autorun reads that model plus session/config state; when eligible it synchronously checks/stores a one-time application flag and displays a notification. Enabling writes two user settings.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Poll PR state used by both the icon and prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No additional request is introduced by the prompt autorun; it consumes the existing designated PR model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The polling contribution already acquired and refreshed PR models for session status icons.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Prompt eligibility waits for existing PR model data, but does not add network work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and persist a one-time prompted flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reads on eligible autorun executions; one successful write application-wide.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cleanup prompt storage flag existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous small storage access before notification display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write archive and delete thresholds to user configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two writes only if the user selects the enable action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No combined cleanup enable action existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User action completes asynchronously; failures are surfaced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tracked non-archived sessions controls cheap observable evaluations, but only one designated PR per session installs the prompt autorun and only one prompt can persist.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One autorun per designated PR tracker. The application storage flag coalesces prompts globally; setting writes run in parallel only after explicit user action.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses existing PR model cache/polling. Application storage durably suppresses repeat prompts. Configuration observable updates suppress prompting when either cleanup threshold is enabled.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that added work is local and bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Observable evaluation frequency depends on session/model changes, but no new network polling or scaling expensive boundary was introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 27 changed files. Submitted two medium-confidence-severity findings: duplicate authoritative GitHub refresh rounds on cleanup-only candidates, and default startup/hourly O(session-history) filesystem/SQLite fan-out. Archive, delete, Git safety, renderer prompt, policy, residency, and cleanup lifecycle paths were traced without additional reportable performance regressions.
